editorial.summary:
Meta has released Muse Wonder, described by The Daily Star and ExtremeTech as its first frontier AI models, in a push to compete with rivals such as OpenAI and Anthropic. AI Insider reported that the release comes from Meta Superintelligence Lab. CXOToday.com referred to two models, Muse Wonder and Wonder Full.

Konsulteer reported that the Muse Wonder models offer long-term memory and advanced coding capabilities. The Daily Star said the model is built to rival GPT and Claude. The Verge wrote that Anthropic and OpenAI had appeared to hold the lead in the AI race, with Google seeming far behind, and that Meta, despite spending billions to revive its AI ambitions, had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. TIKR.com raised the question of whether Meta's capital spending can be paid for.
editorial.whyItMatters: Meta's entry with frontier-level models adds another large lab to the race at the top of AI capability, which could affect the pace of progress toward more powerful systems.
keyFacts: Meta's Muse Wonder is described by The Daily Star and ExtremeTech as its first frontier AI model.
AI Insider reported the models come from Meta Superintelligence Lab.
Konsulteer reported the models include long-term memory and advanced coding capabilities.
CXOToday.com named two models: Muse Wonder and Wonder Full.
editorial.note: Yahoo Finance's report concerns Anthropic reaching a milestone relevant to AI stocks, apparently a different event from Meta's model release.

reports.title: Trump announces creation of Super Intelligence Force in US — Deutsche Welle
Tech Debate: Is it Artificial Intelligence or Super Intelligence?
Super Intelligence: Washington Redefines the Rules
Arctic Wolf CEO Nick Schneider On Frontier AI Guardrails: ‘Right Now They Don’t Have It Figured Out’
Super Intelligence
Trump really wants to make ‘super intelligence’ happen. Is it going to happen?
A Guide to Which AI CEOs Now Say ‘Super Intelligence’ and Which Don’t

editorial.summary:
Gizmodo published a guide tracking which AI company chief executives now use the term "superintelligence" in their public remarks and which avoid it. Other outlets covered the term from different angles. UA.NEWS, citing Deutsche Welle, reported that Trump announced the creation of a Super Intelligence Force in the US. Egypt Independent asked whether Trump's push to make "super intelligence" happen would succeed, and The Jerusalem Strategic Tribune described Washington as redefining the rules around superintelligence. Fast Company South Africa framed a debate over whether the field is artificial intelligence or super intelligence.

CRN carried an interview with Arctic Wolf CEO Nick Schneider on frontier AI guardrails, in which he said that right now frontier AI developers do not have guardrails figured out. A NASA page titled "Super Intelligence" was also among the reports listed for this event.
editorial.whyItMatters: The coverage shows that the word "superintelligence" has become a point of contention among AI leaders and government officials, with differing views on its meaning and use. For AI safety discussions, Schneider's remarks add a view on the state of guardrails for frontier systems.
keyFacts: Gizmodo's guide sorts AI CEOs by whether they say "superintelligence" publicly.
According to UA.NEWS, citing Deutsche Welle, Trump announced the creation of a Super Intelligence Force in the US.
CRN quoted Arctic Wolf CEO Nick Schneider saying frontier AI developers do not yet have guardrails figured out.
editorial.note: The NASA item carries only the title "Super Intelligence" and does not describe the same event as the other reports, so it is not treated as corroborating them.

reports.title: Trump AI Rebrand: Super Intelligence Searches Triple [2026]
Trump administration rolls out SI.gov as part of push to rebrand AI as super intelligence
Which Tech Leaders Are Adopting Trump’s ‘Super Intelligence’ Rebrand?

editorial.summary:
Newsweek asked which technology leaders are adopting the Trump administration's "super intelligence" branding, a question tied to the broader debate over how AI is described. Firstpost reported that the administration rolled out a website, SI.gov, as part of a push to rebrand AI as "super intelligence." Tech-insider.org reported that searches for the term "super intelligence" had tripled, presenting that rise as part of the rebranding effort.

The three outlets frame the story around the same administration initiative, though their emphasis differs: Newsweek focuses on which industry figures are using the new terminology, while Firstpost centers on the government website and Tech-insider.org on search interest.
editorial.whyItMatters: The shift in terminology matters for how the public and policymakers understand the path to superintelligence, AI safety, and the debate over AI's effect on work.
keyFacts: Firstpost reported that the Trump administration launched SI.gov as part of a push to rebrand AI as super intelligence.
Tech-insider.org reported that searches for "super intelligence" had tripled.
Newsweek's report asks which tech leaders are adopting the rebrand.
editorial.note: Newsweek's report centers on which tech leaders are adopting the term, while Firstpost and Tech-insider.org focus on a government website and search volume.
